learn.pageTitle: Riichi Mahjong Fu for the Pair (Jantou)
learn.pageDescription: How the pair adds fu in riichi mahjong: dragon pairs, round and seat wind pairs, and the double wind pair, explained with tile images.
learn.whatIsJantouBody:
The [[jantou|pair]] (jantou) is the two identical tiles ([[toitsu|toitsu]]) that every [[hora|winning]] [[tehai|hand]] contains exactly once.
It is also called the head (atama).
Depending on which tile makes up the pair, it can add fu.
learn.yakuhaiBody:
A pair of [[sangenpai|dragon tiles]] (haku, hatsu, chun) always adds 2 fu.
A pair of [[kazehai|wind tiles]] is also worth 2 fu when the wind is the round wind or your seat wind.
learn.noFuBody: A pair of [[shuupai|number tiles]] or of a [[otakaze|guest wind]] (otakaze) adds no fu.
learn.labelOtakaze: Guest wind (West, in the East round from the South seat)
learn.columnTitle: Fu for a double wind pair (round wind = seat wind)
learn.columnBody:
When the round wind and your seat wind are the same tile (for example, East for the East seat in the East round), that tile is called a double wind.

How many fu a double wind pair adds depends on the rules.

Some rules count it as 2 fu for the round wind plus 2 fu for the seat wind, 4 fu in total, while others give it a flat 2 fu like any other yakuhai pair.

Check which rule is in use before you play.
learn.columnSettingsNote: * In this app you can switch in <settingsLink>Settings</settingsLink> whether a double wind pair counts as 4 fu
